reasons: Status is correctly characterized: Section 14 contains an insurance obligation but only partially meets the playbook (no CGL aggregate, E&O at $1M, no cyber), so a partial-coverage deviation with an in-place amendment is the right treatment rather than an insert.

Redline reaches the preferred position on all three gaps — $1M per occurrence / $2M aggregate CGL, E&O raised to $2M, and cyber liability of $5M — plus the one-year tail and 'at its own expense' from the model language.

Edit is appropriately minimal and directionally correct for the customer: workers' compensation, certificate-on-request and notice-of-material-change provisions are left intact, and the changed-character ratio (0.386) reflects targeted limit amendments rather than a rewrite.

Cyber trigger is sensibly adapted to the document's own vocabulary ('Company data or Confidential Information') because no 'Customer Data' term is defined, and the premises/system-access facts cited justify requiring cyber coverage.
Comment is accurate, states what changed and why, cites the playbook limits, and offers the documented fallback (E&O $1M / cyber $2M) in the correct tone and with the required prefix.

Minor, non-blocking: the 'and for one (1) year thereafter' tail now literally extends to workers' compensation as well, and the counterparty-friendly 'or self-insurance' language was deliberately left unchallenged — both acceptable at this low severity.
